Subject: Two-stage commit proposal — burst year + stability buckets

Hi James —

Great conversation yesterday. Per our call I’m attaching a compact proposal that tries to balance Stratus’ need to accelerate Year 1 capacity for product launches while giving you predictable unit economics in Years 2–3. High level: 

- Year 1 (Burst window): larger upfront commit to cover Q1–Q2 launch and marketing-driven spikes. Upfront credits and a one-time onboarding credit to reduce effective cost during ramp.
- Years 2–3 (Stability buckets): annualized, smaller committed buckets per year that guarantee baseline throughput and lower per-token rates. Buckets are designed to cover 95th percentile steady-state usage.
- Fallback buckets & overage handling: if burst demand subsides we route to stability buckets; if you exceed committed capacity we apply short-term burst credits first, then tiered overage at pre-agreed rates.
- Stability triggers: mechanical conversion rules allow us to convert portion of unused burst into stability capacity at pre-negotiated economics — this avoids renegotiation when product usage normalizes.
- Auto-renew opt-in w/ opt-out window: Years 2+ auto-renew by default to preserve pricing, with a 60-day opt-out window before renewal (we can tighten this if procurement needs).
- SLO rollback & credits: if we miss latency SLOs for >2 consecutive weeks, a partial credit applies to the following invoice.

Attachments: 20261102_Redwood_Proposal_Stratus_v2.pdf (proposal), safety_anchor_playbook.xlsx (operational examples), option_b_pricing_breakdown.csv (detailed numbers).

Ask: please review the proposal and flag any non-starters (auto-renew window, stability trigger mechanics, or the fallbacks). If this looks directionally correct I’ll route a clean DocuSign for procurement and a compact playbook for your SREs.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks for this. I skimmed the PDF and the mechanics look reasonable; a few clarifying questions before I loop legal/procurement: 

1) Pricing: can you confirm the effective $/1000 tokens for (a) burst year (after onboarding credits) and (b) stability bucket for Years 2 & 3? The table in Option B is clear but I want a single-line comparator for our CFO.
2) Auto-renew: our procurement team usually pushes for explicit consent to renew (we rarely do automatic renewals). Is the 60-day opt-out negotiable to a 30-day opt-out and an explicit renewal notification 45 days prior?
3) Conversion triggers: what metric triggers conversion from burst to stability? We need something deterministic (e.g., 90-day rolling average QPS below X).
4) DocuSign/sample contract: can you send a redline-ready DocuSign link or a PDF copy we can route to our procurement/legal?

If you can get me the single-line pricing comparators and confirm the opt-out window options, I’ll get procurement on a call tomorrow afternoon.
